standard_prerequisites.use: Closing line of the proof (source line 1265): by the principle of induction on formulas, every formula has a formation sequence.

core_obligations: Atomic base (proof lines 1234-1236): if A is atomic, the one-term sequence tuple(A) is a formation sequence for A.

The seven construction cases (lines 1238-1262): if B and C have formation sequences (B_0,...,B_n) and (C_0,...,C_m), then for each construction rule a longer sequence is a formation sequence for A: negation appends lnot B_n; conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional append both sequences followed by (B_n \circ C_m); universal and existential quantification append B_n wrapped with the quantifier. Each case is stated and verified by displaying the sequence.
Induction conclusion (lines 1263-1265): by the principle of induction on formulas, every formula A has a formation sequence.
proof_roadmap: Handle the atomic case with the one-term sequence.
Extend formation sequences through the seven formula-building rules.
difficulty_reason: Induction proposition (statement 1230-1232, proof 1234-1267): every formula has a formation sequence - the proof runs the standard induction over the seven construction rules, displaying the extended formation sequence in each case, and closes with the induction principle; no step is omitted. H2: routine induction with explicit case display.
